Rochford's population increased by around 2,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 86,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Rochford increased by 2.9%, from just under 83,300 in 2011 to around 85,700 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Rochford was home to around 3.7 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.6 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 45% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Rochford than across the East of England

An older Rochford

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Rochford increased by two years, from 44 to 46 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 65 to 74 years rose by around 1,500 (an increase of 16.5%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 2,900 (15.7% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 65 and 74 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Rochford stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Rochford, but fell across England.

In Rochford, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 7.6% in 2011 to 8.1% in 2021, while across England it fell from 17.7% to 17.1%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 15.7% to 15.5%.

Private renting in Rochford increased from 8.5% to 10.7%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 82.9% to 80.6%.

The rate of social renting in Rochford increased by 0.5 percentage points

Unpaid care in Rochford

Rochford saw the East of England's joint largest percentage-point fall (alongside Dacorum) in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 8.0% in 2011 to 4.7% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Bedford (from 7.6% to 4.4%), Cambridge (from 7.6% to 4.4%), Brentwood (from 7.9% to 4.7%) and Babergh (from 7.9% to 4.7%) saw the East of England's next largest decreases in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Every local authority area across the East of England saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.3% to 4.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Rochford decreased by 3.3 percentage points

Religion in Rochford

In 2021, 44.9% of Rochford residents reported having "No religion", up from 27.9% in 2011. The rise of 17.1 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Rochford. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 47.6% of people in Rochford described themselves as Christian (down from 63.4%), while 5.5% did not state their religion (down from 7.2% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 44.9% of usual residents in Rochford reported having "No religion"

Marriage and civil partnership in Rochford

Rochford saw the East of England's joint second-largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) (from 55.7% in 2011 to 51.5% in 2021).

Across the region, only Fenland saw a greater fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) (from 50.3% to 45.4%).

Despite the decrease, Rochford was in the highest 20% of English local authority areas for the share of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) in 2021.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Rochford decreased by 4.2 percentage points

Rochford residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 81,000 Rochford residents said they were born in England. This represented 94.6% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 78,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 94.7% of Rochford's population.

Scotland was the next most represented, with just under 650 Rochford residents reporting this country of birth (0.8%). This figure was down from around 700 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.9% of the population of Rochford.

The number of Rochford residents born in Wales fell from just under 500 in 2011 (0.6% of the local population) to around 400 in 2021 (0.5%).

In 2021, 94.6% of Rochford residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Rochford

In 2021, 1.7% of Rochford residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (1.6%).

In 2021, 0.6% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.3% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Rochford that identified as "British only" increased from 12.1% to 54.7%.

This area had the region’s lowest percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. Castle Point had the East of England's next lowest percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK (2.0%), while Cambridge had the region's highest percentage (26.9%).

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Rochford increased by 0.1 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

Of Rochford households, 16.8% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.5% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Rochford (2.7 percentage points) than across the East of England (1.8 percentage points, from 19.0% to 17.2%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Rochford decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Rochford residents aged 16 years and over, 56.4% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 58.2% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 50 people (2.2%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.7% in 2011. The percentage of retired Rochford residents increased from 26.5% to 27.8%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Rochford (1.8 percentage points) than across the East of England (1.1 percentage points, from 58.4% to 57.3%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Rochford decreased by 1.8 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.8% of Rochford residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 11.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in eight people (12.2%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 14.5% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 55.7% to 57.1%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Rochford (0.8 percentage points) than across the East of England (0.4 percentage points, from 10.4% to 10.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Rochford increased by 0.8 percentage points

Disability in Rochford

In 2021, 5.7% of Rochford residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.9% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 11 people (9.3%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.5% in 2011. The proportion of Rochford residents who were not disabled increased from 83.6% to 85.1%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Rochford (1.2 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Rochford decreased by 1.2 percentage points

Health in Rochford

In 2021, 50.7% of Rochford residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 48.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.7% to 34.1%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Rochford residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.3% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Rochford increased by 2.3 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Rochford

In 2021, 1.7% of Rochford residents identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category, up from 1.1% in 2011. The 0.6 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from "Mixed or Multiple ethnic groups" increased from 1.9% to 2.8%, while across England the percentage increased from 2.3% to 3.0%.

In 2021, 95.9% of people in Rochford identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 97.2% in 2011), while 1.4% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 1.1% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 0.5% in 2011 to 0.7% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 1.7% of usual residents in Rochford identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category
